name: shop-duplication
prompt: The exports in package shop.export (Csv.write, Json.write and Markdown.write) leave out pending orders. They must also leave out cancelled orders, and list the orders by customer name, then by ID, instead of by ID alone.

name: shop-tangled
prompt: Add a customer kind "partner" (an Order whose customerKind() is "partner") to Pricing.total in package shop.pricing: partners pay wholesale's unit price (20% off) but get none of the quantity discounts, and they pay tax as retail customers do (20%, or 18% when the subtotal is over 100000 cents). Other customers' prices do not change.

name: shop-currency
prompt: The exports in package shop.export write amounts as dollars and cents. Make them use the shop's currency: add a record shop.export.Currency(String code, String symbol, int decimals), and give Csv.write, Json.write and Markdown.write a second parameter Currency cur. Totals are in the currency's minor units (cents for USD); write them with cur.decimals() decimal places, and with no decimal point when it is 0. Csv and Json write the number alone; Markdown puts cur.symbol() before it, as it does with $ today. With new Currency("USD", "$", 2) the output is what it is now.

name: shop-address
prompt: Orders can now ship abroad, so addresses need a country. Add a record shop.order.Address(String street, String city, String postcode, String country), and give Order a component Address address in place of its street, city and postcode components, so that it is Order(String id, String customer, String customerKind, Address address, Status status, List<Line> lines). Shipping.validAddress takes an Address; it must also report a missing country, and the 5-digit postcode rule applies only when the country is "US". The shipping label ends with the country on a line of its own, except for "US". Everything else, such as the exports, keeps working as before.
